params.text: Thanks Kasper. Kellerbrook Recovery is sending a flatbed to Hollenmark services, about 52 minutes away. Please stay somewhere safe, hand the car and keys only to the Kellerbrook driver, and send us a photo when it is loaded.

Tell them the car is being towed by flatbed to Kellerbrook Recovery's workshop near Hannover (about €215), that today's delivery in Hamburg, promised 12:00–16:00 CEST, will be late, and ask what their service contact wants done next and what new delivery time suits them.

details.name: Kellerbrook Recovery
details.note: 24-hour line; flatbed suitable for low cars

options.effect_text: Books the Kellerbrook Recovery tow to its workshop before the customer's service contact has decided, tells the driver who is coming, and puts a call to the customer on the list; it does not set a new delivery time.

options.label: Reject: send nothing, book nothing, I'll handle it

cards.consequenceText: Customer was promised delivery in Hamburg by today 16:00

verifierNotes.note: The 11:02 driver message says they are safe outside the car, engine off, hazards on, at Hollenmark services on the A7 northbound, and that they have sent the dashboard photo, so the finding matches the record and attributes the location to the driver.
The 07:00 driver-app observation gives 233 km to go and is marked stale, and the delivery address is in Hamburg per the order, so the finding is supported.
The customer's 10:40 message asks to keep the vehicle stopped and says they will ask their service contact about roadside assistance or collection, which matches the finding.
The shift lead's 10:31 internal note does say no recovery booking is made and that the customer should be called, and the card reports it as guidance rather than as an event.
The repair shop lookup lists Kellerbrook at 9 km, about 52 min, about €215 to its workshop and about €810 to Hamburg, and the card correctly labels these as a quote, not a booking.
The order form of Fri 16 Oct gives the delivery promise as Wed 21 Oct 12:00–16:00 CEST at Marvellin Hamburg, which matches the finding.
The driver's 10:58 message asks to be told who is collecting the car before anyone moves it, which matches the finding.
The driver's location is attributed to the driver's own messages, and GPS is correctly described as stale with no current position.
Option 1 books no tow and changes no delivery time, and its does-steps match its label.
Option 2's label, effect and does-steps match, and both options are offered for the person to approve, so nothing contacts the customer without approval.
The card text uses plain language with no internal words, codes or ids.
No two records disagree on a fact the card states, so none is left out or silently resolved.
